questions.prompt: Name a country in Africa.
questions.rule: Name one sovereign country located in Africa. This starter pack verifies the entries listed below; other valid countries may not yet be included.

answers.name: Lesotho
answers.fact: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
answers.explanation: It is an enclave country and the only independent state entirely above 1,000 metres in elevation.

answers.name: Eswatini
answers.fact: Eswatini is one of Africa's smallest countries.
answers.explanation: The country was called Swaziland until 2018; its two capitals are Mbabane and Lobamba.

answers.name: Djibouti
answers.fact: Djibouti sits beside the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
answers.explanation: The strait links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, a major maritime route.

answers.name: Benin
answers.fact: The historic Kingdom of Dahomey was based in present-day Benin.
answers.explanation: Abomey, the former royal capital, is known for its preserved royal palaces.

answers.name: Comoros
answers.fact: Comoros is an island country in the Mozambique Channel.
answers.explanation: Its islands lie between Madagascar and the African mainland in the Indian Ocean.

answers.name: Botswana
answers.fact: Botswana contains much of the Kalahari Desert.
answers.explanation: The Okavango Delta spreads into a vast inland wetland in the country's northwest.

answers.name: Eritrea
answers.fact: Eritrea has a long coastline on the Red Sea.
answers.explanation: Its capital, Asmara, is noted for modernist architecture from the Italian colonial period.

answers.name: Gabon
answers.fact: Large areas of Gabon are covered by tropical rainforest.
answers.explanation: The country is part of the Congo Basin, one of the world's major rainforest regions.

answers.name: Malawi
answers.fact: Lake Malawi is one of Africa's Great Lakes.
answers.explanation: The lake is famous for its exceptionally diverse cichlid fish.

answers.name: Togo
answers.fact: Togo is a narrow country stretching north from the Gulf of Guinea.
answers.explanation: Its capital, Lomé, lies on the Atlantic coast near the border with Ghana.

questions.prompt: Name an island in the Mediterranean Sea.
questions.rule: Name a natural island in the Mediterranean. This pack accepts the listed islands and their aliases.

answers.name: Sardinia
answers.fact: Sardinia is home to thousands of ancient stone nuraghe.
answers.explanation: These distinctive Bronze Age tower structures are found across the Italian island.

answers.name: Corsica
answers.fact: Napoleon Bonaparte was born in Corsica.
answers.explanation: The island is French today, though it has a distinct Corsican language and culture.

answers.name: Crete
answers.fact: Crete was the center of the ancient Minoan civilization.
answers.explanation: The palace complex at Knossos is one of the best-known archaeological sites associated with the Minoans.

answers.name: Rhodes
answers.fact: The Colossus of Rhodes was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
answers.explanation: The enormous bronze statue once stood near the Greek island's ancient harbor.

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Cyprus is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean.
answers.explanation: The island lies at the eastern end of the sea, south of Turkey and west of Syria.

answers.name: Malta
answers.fact: Malta's megalithic temples are older than the Egyptian pyramids.
answers.explanation: Several prehistoric temple sites on the islands are UNESCO World Heritage sites.

answers.name: Sicily
answers.fact: Mount Etna, Europe's most active volcano, is on Sicily.
answers.explanation: The Italian island sits just off the toe of the Italian peninsula.

answers.name: Ibiza
answers.fact: Ibiza is one of the Balearic Islands of Spain.
answers.explanation: Beyond its nightlife, the island has a protected old town and important seagrass meadows.

answers.name: Lesbos
answers.fact: The word 'lesbian' derives from the name of Lesbos.
answers.explanation: The ancient Greek poet Sappho lived on Lesbos; her poetry is associated with love between women.

answers.name: Mallorca
answers.fact: Mallorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands.
answers.explanation: Its Serra de Tramuntana mountain range runs along the island's northwest coast.

questions.prompt: Name a chemical element whose symbol does not start with the same letter as its English name.
questions.rule: Name an element with a chemical symbol derived from a different-language or older name. The accepted entries demonstrate the rule.

answers.name: Sodium
answers.fact: Sodium's symbol, Na, comes from the Latin natrium.
answers.explanation: The symbol preserves an older name rather than the English word sodium.

answers.name: Potassium
answers.fact: Potassium's symbol K comes from the Latin kalium.
answers.explanation: The English name refers to potash, while the symbol reflects another historical name.

answers.name: Iron
answers.fact: Iron's symbol Fe comes from the Latin ferrum.
answers.explanation: Ferrum is also the origin of words such as ferrous and ferric.

answers.name: Copper
answers.fact: Copper's symbol Cu is linked to the Latin cuprum.
answers.explanation: Cuprum is traditionally connected with the metal's association with Cyprus.

answers.name: Silver
answers.fact: Silver's symbol Ag comes from the Latin argentum.
answers.explanation: The same root appears in Argentina's name, traditionally associated with silver.

answers.name: Gold
answers.fact: Gold's symbol Au comes from the Latin aurum.
answers.explanation: Aurum is also the source of the word 'auric,' relating to gold.

answers.name: Mercury
answers.fact: Mercury's symbol Hg comes from the Greek hydrargyrum.
answers.explanation: The old name means 'liquid silver,' reflecting mercury's appearance.

answers.name: Lead
answers.fact: Lead's symbol Pb comes from the Latin plumbum.
answers.explanation: The Latin root survives in words such as plumbing and plumber.

answers.name: Tin
answers.fact: Tin's symbol Sn comes from the Latin stannum.
answers.explanation: The Latin-derived symbol is different from the English element name.

answers.name: Antimony
answers.fact: Antimony's symbol Sb comes from the Latin stibium.
answers.explanation: Its symbol reflects the mineral name used in historical Latin texts.

questions.prompt: Name a moon of a planet other than Earth.
questions.rule: Name a natural satellite orbiting a planet other than Earth. This starter set includes these confirmed moons.

answers.name: Io
answers.fact: Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active world known.
answers.explanation: Tidal forces from Jupiter and neighboring moons heat Io's interior and drive its volcanism.

answers.name: Europa
answers.fact: Europa likely has a global ocean beneath its icy crust.
answers.explanation: Evidence from spacecraft observations makes it a major target in the search for habitable environments.

answers.name: Ganymede
answers.fact: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System.
answers.explanation: Jupiter's moon is larger than the planet Mercury and has its own magnetic field.

answers.name: Callisto
answers.fact: Callisto's surface is among the most heavily cratered in the Solar System.
answers.explanation: This ancient-looking Jupiter moon preserves a record of impacts over billions of years.

answers.name: Titan
answers.fact: Titan has lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane.
answers.explanation: Saturn's largest moon has a dense atmosphere and a weather cycle based on hydrocarbons.

answers.name: Enceladus
answers.fact: Enceladus shoots water-rich plumes into space.
answers.explanation: The plumes erupt from fractures near its south pole and reveal a subsurface ocean.

answers.name: Triton
answers.fact: Neptune's Triton orbits in the direction opposite Neptune's rotation.
answers.explanation: Its retrograde orbit suggests Triton was captured rather than forming alongside Neptune.

answers.name: Phobos
answers.fact: Phobos is slowly spiraling toward Mars.
answers.explanation: The small moon orbits so close to Mars that tidal forces are gradually changing its orbit.

answers.name: Deimos
answers.fact: Deimos is the smaller and more distant of Mars's two moons.
answers.explanation: It is irregularly shaped and was named after the Greek personification of dread.

answers.name: Mimas
answers.fact: Saturn's moon Mimas has a crater that gives it a 'Death Star' appearance.
answers.explanation: The large Herschel crater dominates one hemisphere of this small, icy moon.

questions.prompt: Name an ancient civilization or culture known for a distinctive archaeological achievement.
questions.rule: Give the conventional name of a historical civilization or culture represented below.

answers.name: Minoans
answers.fact: The Minoans built monumental palace complexes on Crete.
answers.explanation: Knossos is the largest and most famous palace site associated with this Bronze Age culture.

answers.name: Hittites
answers.fact: The Hittites built an empire centered in Anatolia.
answers.explanation: Their capital Hattusa is a major archaeological site in modern Turkey.

answers.name: Phoenicians
answers.fact: Phoenician traders spread an early alphabet around the Mediterranean.
answers.explanation: The Phoenician writing system influenced later alphabets, including Greek.

answers.name: Etruscans
answers.fact: The Etruscans flourished in central Italy before Roman dominance.
answers.explanation: Their art, religious practices, and engineering influenced early Roman culture.

answers.name: Nabataeans
answers.fact: The Nabataeans carved monumental buildings at Petra.
answers.explanation: Petra in present-day Jordan was a major center on ancient trade routes.

answers.name: Aksumites
answers.fact: The Kingdom of Aksum minted its own coins in antiquity.
answers.explanation: Aksum was a powerful Red Sea trading state in what is now Ethiopia and Eritrea.

answers.name: Olmecs
answers.fact: Olmec artists carved colossal stone heads in Mesoamerica.
answers.explanation: The heads are among the most recognizable works of the Olmec culture of the Gulf Coast.

answers.name: Moche
answers.fact: Moche artisans made highly detailed portrait vessels.
answers.explanation: The Moche flourished on Peru's north coast long before the Inca Empire.

answers.name: Harappans
answers.fact: Harappan cities used carefully planned streets and drainage systems.
answers.explanation: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were major urban centers of the Indus civilization.

answers.name: Hohokam
answers.fact: The Hohokam built extensive irrigation canals in the Sonoran Desert.
answers.explanation: Their canal networks supported agriculture in what is now Arizona.

questions.prompt: Name a major river in South America.
questions.rule: Name a natural river flowing in South America; accepted entries are listed below.

answers.name: Amazon River
answers.fact: The Amazon carries more water than any other river system.
answers.explanation: Its enormous discharge reaches the Atlantic Ocean and drains a vast rainforest basin.

answers.name: Orinoco River
answers.fact: The Orinoco forms a vast delta in Venezuela.
answers.explanation: It is one of South America's great river systems and partly marks the Venezuela-Colombia border.

answers.name: Paraná River
answers.fact: The Paraná joins the Uruguay River to form the Río de la Plata estuary.
answers.explanation: It is a major waterway shared by Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina.

answers.name: São Francisco River
answers.fact: The São Francisco River flows entirely within Brazil.
answers.explanation: It crosses several Brazilian regions and has long supported transport and agriculture.

answers.name: Magdalena River
answers.fact: The Magdalena is Colombia's principal river artery.
answers.explanation: It flows north through the Andes region to the Caribbean Sea.

answers.name: Uruguay River
answers.fact: The Uruguay River helps form part of the Argentina-Uruguay border.
answers.explanation: It joins the Paraná to form the broad Río de la Plata estuary.

answers.name: Tocantins River
answers.fact: The Tocantins is a major river system in Brazil.
answers.explanation: It flows north toward the Atlantic, though it is separate from the Amazon's main channel.

answers.name: Essequibo River
answers.fact: The Essequibo is Guyana's longest river.
answers.explanation: It flows north through rainforest and savanna to the Atlantic coast.

answers.name: Negro River
answers.fact: The dark-water Negro River meets the sandy Amazon near Manaus.
answers.explanation: The two rivers run side by side for several miles before mixing, creating the Meeting of Waters.

answers.name: Pilcomayo River
answers.fact: The Pilcomayo forms part of the border region between Argentina and Paraguay.
answers.explanation: It is a tributary of the Paraguay River and flows through the Gran Chaco.

questions.prompt: Name a Nobel Prize in Literature laureate.
questions.rule: Name a person who received the Nobel Prize in Literature. The listed entries are verified laureates.

answers.name: Wole Soyinka
answers.fact: Wole Soyinka was the first African awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
answers.explanation: The Nigerian playwright received the prize in 1986.

answers.name: Toni Morrison
answers.fact: Toni Morrison received the Literature Nobel in 1993.
answers.explanation: Her novels include Beloved, which won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

answers.name: Rabindranath Tagore
answers.fact: Rabindranath Tagore was the first non-European Literature laureate.
answers.explanation: The Bengali poet and writer received the prize in 1913.

answers.name: Naguib Mahfouz
answers.fact: Naguib Mahfouz was the first Arabic-language writer to win the Literature Nobel.
answers.explanation: The Egyptian novelist received the award in 1988.

answers.name: Wisława Szymborska
answers.fact: Wisława Szymborska won the Literature Nobel in 1996.
answers.explanation: The Polish poet was praised for poetry that illuminates historical and biological contexts.

answers.name: Derek Walcott
answers.fact: Derek Walcott was a poet and playwright from Saint Lucia.
answers.explanation: He received the Literature Nobel in 1992 and often drew on Caribbean history and culture.

answers.name: Olga Tokarczuk
answers.fact: Olga Tokarczuk received the 2018 Literature Nobel, announced in 2019.
answers.explanation: The Polish novelist's work often uses myth, travel, and unconventional narrative structures.

answers.name: Kazuo Ishiguro
answers.fact: Kazuo Ishiguro was born in Nagasaki and grew up in Britain.
answers.explanation: The novelist received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2017.

answers.name: Annie Ernaux
answers.fact: Annie Ernaux's writing often draws on personal memory and social history.
answers.explanation: The French author received the Literature Nobel in 2022.

answers.name: Abdulrazak Gurnah
answers.fact: Abdulrazak Gurnah was born in Zanzibar and later settled in Britain.
answers.explanation: The novelist received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2021.

questions.prompt: Name a Best Picture Oscar winner from the 1990s.
questions.rule: Name a film that won the Academy Award for Best Picture at a ceremony held from 1990 through 1999 inclusive.

answers.name: Driving Miss Daisy
answers.fact: Driving Miss Daisy won Best Picture at the 62nd Academy Awards.
answers.explanation: The 1989 film received the award at the 1990 ceremony.

answers.name: Dances with Wolves
answers.fact: Dances with Wolves was Kevin Costner's feature directorial debut.
answers.explanation: The film won Best Picture at the 1991 Academy Awards.

answers.name: The Silence of the Lambs
answers.fact: The Silence of the Lambs won the five major Oscar categories.
answers.explanation: It took Best Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, and Adapted Screenplay at the 1992 ceremony.

answers.name: Unforgiven
answers.fact: Unforgiven was directed by and starred Clint Eastwood.
answers.explanation: The western won Best Picture at the 1993 Academy Awards.

answers.name: Schindler's List
answers.fact: Schindler's List was filmed largely in black and white.
answers.explanation: Steven Spielberg's film won Best Picture at the 1994 Academy Awards.

answers.name: Forrest Gump
answers.fact: Forrest Gump won six Academy Awards, including Best Picture.
answers.explanation: The film received Best Picture at the 1995 ceremony.

answers.name: Braveheart
answers.fact: Braveheart won five Oscars, including Best Picture and Director.
answers.explanation: Mel Gibson directed and starred in the 1995 historical epic, honored at the 1996 ceremony.

answers.name: The English Patient
answers.fact: The English Patient won nine Academy Awards.
answers.explanation: Its wins included Best Picture at the 1997 ceremony.

answers.name: Titanic
answers.fact: Titanic tied the record with 11 Academy Award wins.
answers.explanation: The film won Best Picture at the 1998 ceremony.

answers.name: Shakespeare in Love
answers.fact: Shakespeare in Love won Best Picture at the 1999 Academy Awards.
answers.explanation: The film's awards included acting honors for Gwyneth Paltrow and Judi Dench.

questions.prompt: Name a sport that has appeared at the Summer Olympic Games.
questions.rule: Name a sport included in at least one edition of the modern Summer Olympics; this pack provides examples, not an exhaustive list.

answers.name: Tug of war
answers.fact: Tug of war was an Olympic sport from 1900 to 1920.
answers.explanation: It appeared at five Summer Games before being dropped from the programme.

answers.name: Polo
answers.fact: Polo appeared at five Summer Olympics between 1900 and 1936.
answers.explanation: Argentina won the last Olympic polo tournament, at Berlin 1936.

answers.name: Croquet
answers.fact: Croquet was an Olympic event at the 1900 Paris Games.
answers.explanation: It was among the sports included in the early, less standardized Olympic programme.

answers.name: Roque
answers.fact: Roque appeared as an Olympic sport at St. Louis 1904.
answers.explanation: This American court game was a close relative of croquet.

answers.name: Jeu de paume
answers.fact: Jeu de paume was an Olympic sport in 1908.
answers.explanation: The indoor racket sport is an ancestor of modern tennis and is still played by enthusiasts.

answers.name: Lacrosse
answers.fact: Lacrosse was an Olympic medal sport in 1904 and 1908.
answers.explanation: It later appeared as a demonstration sport at several Games.

answers.name: Basque pelota
answers.fact: Basque pelota appeared at the 1900 Paris Olympics.
answers.explanation: Only two teams competed in the medal event, and Spain won.

answers.name: Cricket
answers.fact: Cricket appeared once at the Olympics, at Paris 1900.
answers.explanation: A single match between Great Britain and France determined the medals in the only Olympic cricket tournament so far.

answers.name: Skateboarding
answers.fact: Skateboarding made its Olympic debut at Tokyo 2020.
answers.explanation: The Games took place in 2021 after postponement, but retained the Tokyo 2020 name.

answers.name: Breaking
answers.fact: Breaking made its Olympic debut at Paris 2024.
answers.explanation: The sport's Olympic competition featured B-Boys and B-Girls battles.

questions.prompt: Name a woman who made a notable contribution to science.
questions.rule: Name a scientist represented in the accepted entries. Each entry includes the contribution used to verify the answer.

answers.name: Katherine Johnson
answers.fact: Katherine Johnson calculated trajectories for early U.S. crewed spaceflights.
answers.explanation: Her mathematical work supported missions including John Glenn's 1962 orbital flight.

answers.name: Chien-Shiung Wu
answers.fact: Chien-Shiung Wu led an experiment that demonstrated parity violation.
answers.explanation: Her cobalt-60 experiment tested a prediction by theoretical physicists Lee and Yang.

answers.name: Lise Meitner
answers.fact: Lise Meitner helped explain the physics of nuclear fission.
answers.explanation: Meitner and Otto Frisch interpreted the process after experimental work by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann.

answers.name: Emmy Noether
answers.fact: Emmy Noether's theorem links symmetries with conservation laws.
answers.explanation: The result is a foundational idea in mathematical physics.

answers.name: Rosalind Franklin
answers.fact: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray diffraction work revealed key evidence about DNA's structure.
answers.explanation: Her diffraction image known as Photograph 51 was important to understanding DNA's double helix.

answers.name: Barbara McClintock
answers.fact: Barbara McClintock discovered transposable genetic elements in maize.
answers.explanation: Her work on 'jumping genes' earned the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

answers.name: Tu Youyou
answers.fact: Tu Youyou discovered artemisinin as a treatment for malaria.
answers.explanation: The Chinese scientist shared the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

answers.name: Vera Rubin
answers.fact: Vera Rubin's galaxy-rotation observations provided strong evidence for dark matter.
answers.explanation: Her measurements showed that stars in galaxies moved in ways not explained by visible matter alone.

answers.name: Mary Anning
answers.fact: Mary Anning found important marine fossils on England's Jurassic Coast.
answers.explanation: Her discoveries helped shape early paleontology, though she received little formal recognition during her lifetime.

answers.name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell
answers.fact: Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovered the first radio pulsars as a graduate student.
answers.explanation: Her 1967 observations revealed a new class of rapidly rotating neutron stars.

questions.prompt: Name an author who published under a pen name.
questions.rule: Name a writer known to have published work under the listed pseudonym or pen name.

answers.name: George Eliot
answers.fact: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans.
answers.explanation: She used a male pseudonym in part to have her serious literary work judged independently of gender expectations.

answers.name: Mark Twain
answers.fact: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens.
answers.explanation: The name came from a riverboat sounding meaning two fathoms deep.

answers.name: Lewis Carroll
answers.fact: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of mathematician Charles Dodgson.
answers.explanation: Dodgson wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland under his better-known literary name.

answers.name: Dr. Seuss
answers.fact: Dr. Seuss was the pen name of Theodor Geisel.
answers.explanation: Geisel also used the name Theo LeSieg for books whose illustrations were by other artists.

answers.name: George Orwell
answers.fact: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair.
answers.explanation: He adopted the name before publishing Down and Out in Paris and London.

answers.name: Saki
answers.fact: Saki was the pen name of British writer H. H. Munro.
answers.explanation: He became known for witty, often sharply ironic short stories.

answers.name: Ellis Bell
answers.fact: Emily Brontë first published poetry as Ellis Bell.
answers.explanation: The Brontë sisters initially used gender-ambiguous pen names for their writing.

answers.name: Currer Bell
answers.fact: Charlotte Brontë published Jane Eyre as Currer Bell.
answers.explanation: She and her sisters used pen names beginning with the same initials as their real names.

answers.name: R. K. Narayan
answers.fact: R. K. Narayan shortened his long birth name for his author name.
answers.explanation: His novels often feature the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi.

answers.name: O. Henry
answers.fact: O. Henry was the pen name of American short-story writer William Sydney Porter.
answers.explanation: He became especially associated with twist endings in stories such as The Gift of the Magi.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument in the string family.
questions.rule: Name an instrument whose sound is produced by vibrating strings; the listed entries are accepted examples.

answers.name: Erhu
answers.fact: The erhu is a two-stringed bowed instrument from China.
answers.explanation: Its bow hair passes between the two strings, making the instrument distinctive to play.

answers.name: Kora
answers.fact: The kora is a West African bridge-harp with a large calabash resonator.
answers.explanation: A traditional kora commonly has 21 strings and is associated with Mandinka musical traditions.

answers.name: Sitar
answers.fact: The sitar is a plucked string instrument associated with Hindustani classical music.
answers.explanation: Its sympathetic strings resonate along with the melody strings.

answers.name: Balalaika
answers.fact: The balalaika is a Russian string instrument with a triangular body.
answers.explanation: The family includes instruments of different sizes and registers.

answers.name: Guzheng
answers.fact: The guzheng is a Chinese plucked zither with movable bridges.
answers.explanation: Players can alter pitch by pressing the strings on the left side of the bridges.

answers.name: Mbira
answers.fact: The mbira makes sound with metal tines attached to a wooden board.
answers.explanation: It is strongly associated with Shona music in Zimbabwe and is often played inside a resonator.

answers.name: Bandoneon
answers.fact: The bandoneon is a type of concertina strongly associated with Argentine tango.
answers.explanation: It is played by expanding and compressing its bellows while pressing buttons.

answers.name: Nyckelharpa
answers.fact: The nyckelharpa is a Swedish keyed string instrument.
answers.explanation: Keys press tangents against strings to change pitch while the strings are bowed.

answers.name: Oud
answers.fact: The oud is a fretless lute central to many Middle Eastern musical traditions.
answers.explanation: Its short neck and pear-shaped body distinguish it from many European lutes.

answers.name: Hurdy-gurdy
answers.fact: A hurdy-gurdy sounds when a hand-cranked wheel bows its strings.
answers.explanation: Keys shorten the melody strings while the wheel continuously rubs against them.

questions.prompt: Name a global brand whose name has an interesting origin or former identity.
questions.rule: Name one of the listed companies or brands; the explanation gives the specific name/history connection.

answers.name: IKEA
answers.fact: IKEA is an acronym built from its founder's initials and places in Sweden.
answers.explanation: The letters stand for Ingvar Kamprad, Elmtaryd (his family farm), and Agunnaryd (his home parish).

answers.name: LEGO
answers.fact: LEGO comes from the Danish phrase 'leg godt,' meaning 'play well.'
answers.explanation: The company says the name was formed from the first letters of the two Danish words.

answers.name: Sony
answers.fact: Sony's name combines a Latin word and an English slang word.
answers.explanation: The company explains the name using sonus, meaning sound, and sonny, a familiar term for a young man.

answers.name: Adidas
answers.fact: Adidas is named after its founder, Adolf 'Adi' Dassler.
answers.explanation: The brand name combines his nickname Adi with the beginning of his surname.

answers.name: Pepsi
answers.fact: Pepsi-Cola was created by pharmacist Caleb Bradham.
answers.explanation: Bradham first sold the drink as Brad's Drink in North Carolina before renaming it Pepsi-Cola.

answers.name: Nokia
answers.fact: Nokia began as a Finnish pulp mill company in the 19th century.
answers.explanation: It later moved through several industries before becoming known worldwide for telecommunications.

answers.name: Nintendo
answers.fact: Nintendo began in 1889 making handmade playing cards.
answers.explanation: The Japanese company later expanded into toys and video games.

answers.name: Shell
answers.fact: Shell's emblem was inspired by a real seashell business connection.
answers.explanation: The Shell Transport and Trading Company was named after Marcus Samuel's family business in seashells.

answers.name: Canon
answers.fact: Canon's first camera prototype was called Kwanon.
answers.explanation: The name referenced Kannon, the Buddhist bodhisattva of compassion; the company later adopted Canon.

answers.name: Starbucks
answers.fact: Starbucks was named after a character in the novel Moby-Dick.
answers.explanation: Starbuck is the first mate aboard the Pequod in Herman Melville's novel.

questions.prompt: Name a UNESCO World Heritage Site outside Europe.
questions.rule: Name a site currently inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List outside Europe. Accepted entries have individual UNESCO pages.

answers.name: Taj Mahal
answers.fact: The Taj Mahal was built as a mausoleum commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
answers.explanation: The white-marble complex in Agra was completed in the 17th century.

answers.name: Machu Picchu
answers.fact: Machu Picchu stands high in the Andes of Peru.
answers.explanation: The Inca site combines monumental architecture with a dramatic mountain setting.

answers.name: Petra
answers.fact: Petra's famous Al-Khazneh facade was carved into sandstone.
answers.explanation: The Nabataean city was an important center on ancient trade routes in present-day Jordan.

answers.name: Great Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Great Zimbabwe was built from carefully fitted stone blocks without mortar.
answers.explanation: The medieval city was a major center of the Shona civilization.

answers.name: Angkor
answers.fact: Angkor was the capital region of the Khmer Empire.
answers.explanation: Its temple complex includes Angkor Wat, one of the world's largest religious monuments.

answers.name: Galápagos Islands
answers.fact: The Galápagos Islands helped inspire Charles Darwin's thinking about species.
answers.explanation: Their distinctive wildlife and ecosystems are protected as a World Heritage site.

answers.name: Rapa Nui National Park
answers.fact: Rapa Nui is famous for its monumental moai statues.
